results.title: True pricing – guiding consumers within a new pricing paradigm
results.content: Here, we present the results of a large-scale survey experiment with 1400 Dutch and Danish consumers, investigating the effect of the true price presentation format (absolute, relative or no information) on consumers’ choices. In specific, we investigate the effect of different price presentation formats on consumers’ choices accounting for consumers’ price-quality schema and understanding of true pricing. For true pricing to support consumers in making more sustainable choices at the point of sale, the information provided must at least be easy and fast to comprehend. Evidence from the existing market trials at Penny or Albert Heijn suggests that when hidden costs are communicated as absolute price premiums, it increases consumers’ focus on the overall true price and the sense that products are generally becoming more expensive (Stein et al., 2024. Journal of Marketing Research, 30(2), 234–245.")), consumers’ price quality schema was measured based on the level of agreement with four items on a 7-point Likert scale after the choice experiment.

results.title: Consumer Outlook: Guide to 2026 - NIQ
results.content: ![Image 8: A chart showing the Consumer outlook 2026​ summary of top concerns for global shoppers](https://nielseniq.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2025/09/03.png). ![Image 10: A chart showing the Consumer outlook 2026​ summary of how inflation has impacted global regions](https://nielseniq.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2025/09/11_Elevated-prices-are-squeezing-consumer-wallets-and-reinforcing-that-we-are-in-a-long-term-recovery-period-1.jpg). ![Image 11: A chart showing the Consumer outlook 2026​ summary of regional value sales and volume growth](https://nielseniq.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2025/09/12_Global-growth-persists-but-shows-signs-of-softening-heading-into-2026.jpg). In leading markets like the United States, [NIQ’s Expanded Omnishopper](https://nielseniq.com/global/en/products/expanded-omnishopper/)data proves that **this positive consumer sentiment is clearly impacting spending.**The dollar spend per US household per year is up across major departments, most notably with Health & Beauty products (**+8%**), Baby Care (**+7%**), Food (**+4%**), Pet Care (**+4%**), and Household Care products (**+3%**). ![Image 37: A chart showing the Consumer outlook 2026​ summary of channel value performance](https://nielseniq.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2025/09/37_Global-FMCG-channel-value-performance.jpg). ![Image 38: A chart showing the Consumer outlook 2026​ summary of channel value performance](https://nielseniq.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2025/09/37_Global-FMCG-channel-value-performance-1.jpg). A large portion of this growth is driven by consumer perception that[many products within the private label category are highly substitutable with branded products.](https://nielseniq.com/global/en/insights/report/2025/finding-harmony-on-the-shelf/) Consumers are also no longer shopping private label only because it’s more affordable.
